Inside Macintosh: AppleScript Language Guide / Part 3 - Appendixes
Appendix A - The Language at a Glance

References

A reference is a phrase that specifies an object. Table A-2 summarizes the reference forms you can use to specify objects in AppleScript. The first
column lists the name of the reference form. The second column lists the
syntax for that form.

When you use references to specify objects, you can specify a series of containers, each of which is itself a reference, to identify the object uniquely.
Table A-3 lists the ways to specify containers.

For examples and more detailed descriptions of the AppleScript reference forms, see Chapter 5, "Objects and References."
